## Welcome/ Roll Call

Some technical audio issues were sorted out. Meeting began at 6:39 a.m. PT.

## Review and Adopt Agenda

## Motion

:

## Review and Adopt Draft Minutes

## Motion :

- S. Harrison motions to adopt Sep 24, 2024 minutes.
- L. Marx seconds.
- All members present voted in favor; no one abstained; motion carried.

## Updates

Executive Committee Update- Chair Terranova updates commission on the current status of the compact and the commission's work.

- Rules Committee is working on rules. There are drafts but nothing has become a rule yet besides Rule on Rulemaking. Good discussion and desire to get it right.
- Thanks to partners, NCCPA and AAPA, who are providing funding and act as ex-officios. So far states do not have to pay to be in the compact.
- See PACompact.org for information and map of states that have joined.
- Legislative Update- Carl Sims (CSG) provides a legislative update. 28

- 17 states with filed legislation, 12 still pending

- 3 enacted (now 16 total)
- o Arkansas

- o Montana
- Typical trajectory for licensure compacts
- This work is done in close partnership with AAPA efforts (advocacy, coordinating in-state support)

Committee Reports: Communications- Communications Chair Jean Fischer updates about committee. There have been four meetings, great progress, a great committee with differing viewpoints. Rules- Chair Terranova updates that the rules committee will pick up with the chair coming back soon. Finance- Finance Chair Larry Marx updates that a draft budget has been approved by Finance Committee to be approved by full committee today. Thanks to the funding partners.

## Budget and Funding

- L. Marx updates that the funding MOUs between the Commission, AAPA, NCCPA and CSG are finalized and walks through the draft budget.
- Funds from NCCPA, AAPA, HRSA Grant (through FSMB)
- Fiscal year set at Oct 1 - Sep 30
- Budget has a tab showing how much of the budget is allocated for remaining fiscal year, May Sep 30
- CSG assistance allocated in the budget

Question- J. Fischer asks How will fees work? The goal is that the PA user will pay the fee. The commission is authorized to charge a state assessment fee but the commission hopes to avoid that if possible.

## Motion

:

- L. Marx motions to adopt draft budget.
- J. Alley seconds.
- All members present voted in favor; no one abstained; motion carried.

## Data System

Data System Introduction- C. Sims gives an overview of the need for a data system and the authorization to create one in the compact legislation. Data System Informational Demonstrations

- CompactConnect- Isabel Eliassen (CSG), Stacy Griffin (InspiringApps), Brad Weber (InspiringApps)
- o Project between OT, ASLP, and Counseling Compacts in partnership with CSG
- o Expected to be launched late Summer/early Fall 2025

Questions: J. Alley: Who issues the privilege? No action required by the privilege state to issue the privilege. Home/qualifying state uploads eligible practitioners. Some states require a report to add privilege holders into their own state systems.

- J. Fischer: Two factor authorization? Yes, it's disabled in the system demo

## Delegate Questions and Comments

- J. Fischer: To NCCPA, would an NCCPA data system have a public facing option? If needed yes.

## Public Questions and Comments

Online Question Tamara Dolphens, Nebraska: Can the system be individualized so that PAs with redflags (per the home state) can be discussed by the licensing committee?  For example, a PA who lost privileges or previous disciplinary action on a license in another state would be reviewed directly by a live committee.  Is there built in or automated stop-gap? The commission does not review licensure or have authority to do so. It will be the qualifying state that reviews and submits a licensee for eligibility.
